decision.question: how to resize columns

decision.chose: ext/grip, from: "start" on each header cell
decision.why: law 6 — one resize mechanism on the site, not a second; grip's from:"start" measures the cell's own left edge, which IS the column's start, so write(px) is already the column width with no extra math

options: a bespoke :has()-based master-detail CSS (core/new/1/site/compound/master-detail's own pattern)
decision.why: law 6 — columns() is the system three other pages already use for exactly this shape (core/Page/overview/columns/uses/inbox/); Panel2.Side is navigation chrome that slides OVER the page, not a second reading pane beside it; fill yields to an open child for free, giving the peek with zero new CSS or JS

findings.text: review/diff.patch is empty (0 bytes): the work is uncommitted in the working tree on michael/dev, so the patch captured nothing, and review.jsonl's earlier "size none, pass, cost 0" line reviewed nothing either. This review read `git diff` of the working tree instead; the review packager should diff the working tree, not HEAD.

All three asks are met: a six-column CSS grid with `--col-*` tokens and `minmax()` floors (ai/sessions/sessions.css:35-45), a grip that writes only its own token (ai/sessions/page.js:68-77), the routed detail kept, `load_transcript()` as the one seam (page.js:225), and the house rule in ext/panel2/readme.md:87 plus doc/preview-levels.md. The side peek uses `core/Page` `columns()` instead of the drawer the owner named. The reason is recorded in task.jsonl: the drawer slides over the page, while columns() opens a pane beside it. That reads as a sound reason under law 4, but the owner said "drawer", so it is worth one line on the card.

The grid never grows past the sum of its tokens (about 48.5rem plus gaps), because each track is `minmax(min, var(--col-x))` (sessions.css:38-44). On a `width: "fill"` page at 1920 or 3440, the grid sits at the left with empty space beside it. A `1fr` filler track after Cost, or `max()` on the Name track, would let it use the room without breaking the one-token rule.

Between the 30em stacked fallback and the grid's minimum width (about 37rem plus five gaps), the grid is wider than the panel. `.panel2-main`'s `overflow: auto` turns that into a horizontal scroll inside the panel rather than a broken page. That is acceptable, but nobody checked it at those widths (roughly 480–620px of panel).
The empty state `p.c("muted", "No sessions with an id yet.")` (page.js:192) becomes a grid item, so it is squeezed into the 7rem Start column. It needs `grid-column: 1 / -1`.
A dead rule is left behind: `.sessions-list { }` (sessions.css:26). The class is no longer rendered anywhere, so the rule and its comment can go.

Each row is an `<a>` styled `display: contents` (sessions.css:48). Older Safari versions dropped such links from keyboard focus and the accessibility tree. Current browsers are fine, so this only matters if the site supports old Safari.
